ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Under the PCMLTFA and SOR/2002-184, the filing agent and any financial intermediary must establish and maintain a prescribed risk-based compliance program. Before consenting to act, the limited partnership must screen every general partner, limited partner, authorized signatory, and individual beneficial owner holding 25% or more against Canada's list of politically exposed persons (both domestic and foreign), FINTRAC guidance, Canada's Listed Terrorist Entities under the Criminal Code, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Special Economic Measures Act regulations, OFAC's SDN list and 50% ownership rule, and HM Treasury and EU consolidated financial sanctions where payment processing requires it. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP, family member or close associate, or residence in a high-risk jurisdiction. Because the commercial model relies on Apple App Store and Google Play payouts, all payment and account structures must also comply with OFAC and U.S. sanctions requirements as a condition of the payout rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services (BC Corporate Online / OneStop Business Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must use the Latin alphabet and may contain English or French legal terminology, including acceptable accented characters. If a partner requests a Chinese-language name, the Chinese characters are not registrable as the legal name; only a romanized transliteration or an English/French translation may be used. The name of the limited partnership must include the legal element 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'Société en commandite', or 'S.E.C.' as required under the BC Partnership Act, and must be distinguishable from all existing names in the BC corporate registry, including names reserved, registered, amalgamated, continued, or reinstated.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed once for an additional 56 days by filing a renewal request before expiry. If the Registrar of Companies rejects a name, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal within 30 days of the rejection notice, along with a revised name request, a NUANS or BC name search report, and written submissions demonstrating distinguishability and compliance with the BC naming regulations. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, and may file a new name reservation with payment of a fresh statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office with a physical street address in British Columbia and a registered agent available to accept legal process is permissible for a BC limited partnership, provided it is not a bare post office box or mail-forwarding arrangement. For an ISIC 5820 MMORPG software publishing company, a pure virtual office may be tolerated for registration but should be supplemented with demonstrable commercial substance, such as a local accounting or tax representation office, a hosted server arrangement, or local administrative personnel, to satisfy financial institution due diligence and global payout provider expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; the projected annualized likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the Registrar or by a financial institution is approximately 5%. The likelihood increases to approximately 15% if annual reports are filed inconsistently, the registered office is solely a virtual mail-drop, or tax registration with the Canada Revenue Agency and BC authorities is not substantiated.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, Part 2 (Limited Partnerships), ss. 51-76; Partnership Regulation, BC Reg 380/2003
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Online Portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP1) filed via Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account mandated for British Columbia limited partnerships. Limited partners must contribute consideration fixed by the partnership agreement, which remains a private contract; only the general partner's name and registered address are disclosed to the registry. Public filing fees: CAD 50 for the Declaration of Limited Partnership and optional CAD 30 for name reservation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner hereby approves and adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement for the Partnership, and authorizes the initial Limited Partner to subscribe for its limited partnership interests upon the capital contributions set out in Schedule A, no minimum paid-up capital being required by the Partnership Act (British Columbia). RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership be established at the address recorded in the Declaration of Limited Partnership, and that all statutory filings incident to formation be executed. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the General Partner appoints the Chief Executive Officer and Corporate Secretary named in the minutes, with full authority to file the Declaration of Limited Partnership, annual reports, and to open bank accounts and digital distribution merchant accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Approval and Reservation (NUANS Search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Corporate Online (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Approval Request through Corporate Online, providing three proposed names in order of priority. Attach the most recent NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report dated within 90 days. The registrar will compare the proposed name against existing BC corporate and limited partnership names, trade marks, and distinctive marks to ensure the name is distinguishable and does not falsely imply connection with any government institution. Within 5 business days of name approval, pay the CAD 30 reservation fee to secure the name for 56 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit an amended request with alternative names via Corporate Online; reconsideration of a rejected name may be sought by written submission to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days, citing as justification any trade-mark registrations or long-standing operating goodwill.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Governance Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and founding Limited Partner in private capacity, advised by legal counsel (instrument is not filed with the registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a full Limited Partnership Agreement addressing capital contribution schedules, profit and loss sharing percentages, distribution waterfall, management authority of the general partner, limited partner's non-participation in control (s. 52 of the Partnership Act), transfer restrictions, dissolution events, and governing law (British Columbia). Simultaneously adopt an internal governance charter covering officer roles, signatory authority, banking and payment-rail mandates (Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console payout accounts), and record-keeping duties. The agreement should be executed by all partners and notarized where required by counterparty financial institutions.
required_dossiers: General Partner resolution approving the agreement
Certified copies of partners' identification and proof of authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a financial institution or tax authority questions the partnership terms, amend the agreement by a deed of variation executed by all partners; retroactive amendments on capital accounts are permissible under s. 63 of the Partnership Act if in writing and consented to by the affected partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services — Registrar of Companies via Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Declaration of Limited Partnership, stating the exact reserved partnership name, the registered office address in British Columbia, the name and business address of the general partner, and the general partner's declaration that the partnership is not a restricted business requiring extraprovincial license. Attach the name reservation certificate and pay the CAD 50 filing fee using the Corporate Online credited account. Upon registration, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Limited Partnership; register the certificate in the partnership's minute book.
required_dossiers: General Partner's consent to act and statement of disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the declaration (e.g., defective name, incomplete general partner particulars), the filer shall submit a written explanation and, if necessary, file an Amended Declaration under s. 61(1) of the Partnership Act. Where the query arises from incorrect information, a correction may be filed under s. 62 with the prescribed fee and an affidavit of mistake.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Federal/Provincial Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance (PST and payroll matters)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership with CRA using the Business Number (BN) application, selecting the partnership registration type. Obtain a separate BN program account for GST/HST where the partnership's worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 annually; the partnership will elect to register and collect tax at applicable rates. Register for BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) if taxable software or digital goods are supplied in BC, and commence CRA payroll deductions if employees are hired. The general partner must maintain CRA Form RC4060 (tax account information) and report partnership income allocations under T5013 slips.
required_dossiers: CRA Business Number application (RC1 or online)
Limited Partnership Agreement extract showing general partner authority
Authorized signatory list for CRA and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA placing the BN application under review or requesting clarification, provide the Certificate of Limited Partnership and the executed governance resolution within 30 days; delayed registration may be retroactive to the date of incorporation where the delay was due to CRA processing backlogs and a written request is made through CRA's Business Window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Physical Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Vancouver (or applicable British Columbia municipal licensing department) and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Business Licence application to the municipal licensing office for the partnership's registered and physical operating location, indicating the lease status, occupancy classification, and fire safety compliance. Obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire department for office premises, ensure the workplace meets the BC Building Code occupancy requirements, and register with WorkSafeBC as an employer for occupational health and safety coverage. Post the municipal business licence conspicuously at the registered place of business.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of premises authorization
Certificate of Limited Partnership and BN confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality conditions or denies the licence, the partnership may appeal to the City's Property Use and Business Licence Hearing Board or, alternatively, relocate the operational office to a compliant zone; WorkSafeBC enforcement orders may be remedied by abatement plans submitted within 30 days with progressive penalty provisions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City of Vancouver — Business Licensing Department (or applicable BC municipality); British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (oversight only)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Licence (Municipal) pursuant to the Vancouver Charter, SBC 1953, c. 55, and Business Licence By-law 4450

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy — Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categorically Exempt — Class 2 (No Physical Works). The activity is a digital content publishing operation with no manufacturing, no land disturbance, and no point-source discharges; therefore it is excluded from full Environmental Assessment under the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2018, c. 51.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge; compliance with municipal sanitary sewer bylaws for sanitary sewage. Zero volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from production processes. Electronic waste (servers, IT equipment, batteries) must be recycled under the Recycling Regulation, B.C. Reg. 449/2004 (Environmental Management Act), requiring stewardship of electronic products. Office operations shall comply with the BC Ambient Air Quality Objectives for any minor heating plant and the Municipal Wastewater Regulation, B.C. Reg. 288/2004, where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the local fire department following inspection of means of egress, fire extinguishers, and occupancy load; structural load inspection by a professional engineer where server rooms or heavy equipment are installed; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance for office ergonomics, electrical safety, and emergency response planning under the Workers Compensation Act, RSBC 2019, c. 1 and the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal GST/HST and income tax administration; portal: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO). British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is administered separately by the BC Ministry of Finance (eTaxBC / BC Online portal). Corporate and partnership registration: BC Corporate Online (OneStop BC) under the Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Limited Partnership under the BC Partnership Act via BC Corporate Online; obtain the BC LP registration number and general-partner particulars. Step 2: Apply to CRA for the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts using Form RC1 or Business Registration Online (BRO). A BC LP typically requires the RT program account (GST/HST), plus RC (income tax) and RP (payroll) accounts where applicable; the partnership is the registered person in its own name and must file T5013 Summary and T5013 information slips. Step 3: Non-resident partners must disclose their foreign TIN to the partnership; a non-resident partner may file the ITA s. 216.1 election to pay Part I tax on net Canadian-source partnership business income instead of Part XIII withholding on gross distributions. Step 4: Foreign corporate partners with no Canadian residence obtain a non-resident BN by submitting RC1, a certified certificate of existence, the partnership agreement, and Form RC24 (authorized representative) to the CRA International and Large Business Directorate; issuance typically takes 15–30 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — a BC Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent for federal and BC income tax under ITA s. 96: the partnership computes income or loss as if it were a separate person but pays no entity-level income tax; each partner (individual, corporation, or trust, resident or non-resident) is taxed on its allocated share for the partnership fiscal period. For GST/HST, the partnership is itself a 'person' under ETA s. 123(1) and may register in its own name; each general and limited partner is jointly and severally liable for the partnership's GST/HST debts (ETA s. 272.1). The MMORPG publishing scope (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210) is an ordinary digital software business with a Low_Risk_Standard AML tier and no statutory licence requirement. BC PST registration (7%) is required only for taxable sales of prewritten software consumed in BC; export-only digital supply is PST-exempt.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box entity classification election. Elections available to a BC LP include: (1) partnership fiscal-period election under ITA s. 96(3) to adopt a non-calendar year-end with partner consent; (2) ITA s. 216.1 election for non-resident partners to be taxed on net Canadian-source partnership business income; (3) GST/HST annual or quarterly filing elections and the 'quick method' election for small suppliers (ETA s. 301); (4) ETA s. 156 election for closely related registrants to treat intercompany supplies as made for no consideration, and registration under ETA s. 272 enabling the LP to file a single consolidated GST/HST return as a partnership; (5) hybrid-mismatch neutrality rules under ITA ss. 18.4(3)–(4), which apply automatically where a non-resident partner's home jurisdiction treats the Canadian LP as opaque (BEPS Action 2), with no blanket exemption election but possible CRA consequential adjustments; (6) late-filed elections may be accepted under ITA s. 220(2.1) fairness relief upon penalty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus, in British Columbia, a separate 7% Provincial Sales Tax (PST); BC is not a harmonized province, so HST does not apply in CA-BC. MMORPG digital content supplied for use in BC attracts 5% GST and 7% PST on prewritten software; exports to non-residents are zero-rated for GST and PST-exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148: aggregate worldwide taxable supplies (goods, services, and intangible digital property, excluding financial supplies) over the current and previous three consecutive calendar quarters. A BC LP whose worldwide revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 must register for GST/HST and charge 5% GST on Canadian in-app purchases. Non-resident suppliers of digital services to Canadians are subject to the simplified foreign-supplier registration regime (effective 2021-07-01) once their worldwide digital-supply revenue exceeds CAD 30,000 in any 12-month period; the Canadian-resident LP uses the standard four-quarter test. Voluntary registration below the threshold is permitted but binds the LP to collect GST for 12 months and bars de-registration for 2 years.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API-based stamping, or digital stamp regime exists in Canada or British Columbia. The CRA accepts electronic invoices in any machine-readable format (PDF, XML, JSON, EDI ANSI X12) provided the content requirements of ETA ss. 169–170 and the record-keeping rules of ETA s. 286 are met (vendor name, BN, invoice date, description, consideration, tax rate, and GST amount). The Pan-Canadian e-invoicing framework (PEPPOL BIS 3.0) is voluntary; Quebec's phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing (announced for 2024–2027) does not apply to BC. For platform-mediated MMORPG sales, Apple App Store and Google Play payout reports function as the de facto commercial and tax invoice records; the LP should maintain consolidated e-invoices for business-to-business software licensing and digital ledgers for CRA inspection.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A BC LP may apply the 0% GST export rate to: (i) supplies of intangible personal property (MMORPG software licences, virtual items, in-app purchases) made to non-resident persons for use wholly outside Canada under ETA Schedule VI, Part III, s. 10; and (ii) services supplied to non-residents under ETA s. 23(2) and Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7, provided the service is not performed in Canada or made for use in Canada. Revenue sourced through Apple/Google platforms is treated as supply to the non-resident end user; the LP must attribute each transaction to a foreign jurisdiction using IP geolocation, billing address, and app-store territory reports. Supplies to Canadian end users attract 5% GST and, where taxable, 7% PST on prewritten software. A zero-rated exporter files the GST/HST return (GST34) and may claim input tax credits (ITCs) on development, cloud-hosting, and marketing costs; refunds arise where ITCs exceed output GST. CRA may require security or withhold refunds where supporting export documentation is deficient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A via CBSA/CERS) — required only for tangible media physically shipped from Canada (e.g., collector's editions); pure digital downloads are not customs-reportable

Bill of Lading or air waybill — required only for physical exports; for digital MMORPG delivery, retain Apple/Google payout reports, server delivery logs, and content-delivery-network logs as the shipping equivalent

Inward Remittance Certificate — Canada does not issue a statutory inward remittance certificate; the equivalent evidence is SWIFT MT103 advices, foreign-currency bank statements, and app-store payout reports demonstrating conversion into CAD
Apple App Store and Google Play payout statements (monthly financial reports) showing app identifier, territory-wise net revenue, store commissions, FX rates, and CAD settlement amounts
End-user licence agreement (EUA), MMORPG terms of service, and IP licensing agreements evidencing the grant of digital rights to non-resident users and the non-Canadian place of use
IP-geolocation logs, billing-address records, and storefront country-availability settings evidencing that each transaction's destination is outside Canada
T5013 Partnership Information Return, partner allocation schedules, and intercompany agreements (where a foreign distribution affiliate is used) supporting the zero-rated export sales ledger
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline for export proceeds; the 180-day figure is a receivables best-practice benchmark aligned with CRA's ordinary reassessment cycle. Risk exposure: (1) Reassessment — CRA may extend the standard four-year reassessment window to ten years where misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default (ETA s. 298), recovering uncollected 5% GST plus compounded daily prescribed arrears interest. (2) Civil penalties — failure to file or remit: ETA s. 280 (5% plus 1% per month up to 12 months); false statements or gross negligence: ETA s. 285 (25% of the misstated amount) and ITA s. 163.2 for income-tax misrepresentations; tax evasion: fines of 50%–250% of the tax sought to be evaded, up to CAD 100,000 on summary conviction or CAD 500,000 on indictment, with imprisonment up to 2 years (summary) or 5 years (indictable) (ETA ss. 327–330). (3) GAAR — artificial arrangements inflating export zero-rating are attackable under ETA s. 274, and ITA s. 247 transfer-pricing penalties apply where a foreign distribution affiliate is interposed. (4) Partnership exposure — ETA s. 272.1 renders each general and limited partner jointly and severally liable for the LP's GST/HST debts, materially eroding limited-liability protection in fraudulent zero-rating cases. (5) Mitigation — retain complete export substantiation for at least six years, obtain CRA advance rulings for novel platform structures, and file the GST/HST return with full digital-export evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) under the Bank of Canada Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. B-2). Canada does not operate a dedicated Foreign Exchange Administration or exchange-control licensing authority; foreign-exchange restrictions were abolished, and the Minister of Finance holds only dormant emergency powers through the Exchange Fund Account (Currency, Exchange and Special Powers Act), which are not activated. The practical compliance authorities are FINTRAC (Anti-Money Laundering / Counter-Terrorist Financing), Global Affairs Canada (economic sanctions), the Canada Border Services Agency (cross-border currency reporting), and Statistics Canada (balance-of-payments data collection).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility as an IMF Article VIII member and does not impose exchange controls, profit-remittance licensing, investment screening by currency, or CAD conversion requirements on a British Columbia Limited Partnership. Non-resident limited partners may contribute capital in CAD, USD, EUR or any convertible currency and may receive distributions, capital withdrawals and liquidation proceeds without Bank of Canada or Department of Finance approval. The only practical hurdles are: (i) standard bank-level suitability and sanctions screening; (ii) possible Part XIII Income Tax Act withholding on passive-type remittances (interest, royalties, rents) at 25% or reduced treaty rates, while ordinary active-business allocations and return-of-capital payments to non-resident partners are not subject to withholding; (iii) non-resident partners remain taxable on Canadian-source active-business income and must file the required Canadian returns or claim treaty relief; and (iv) enhanced due-diligence documentation when the ownership chain is non-resident or complex.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian federal law imposes no statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation obligation for export proceeds or cross-border revenue. A BC Limited Partnership publishing hardcore MMORPG titles may retain all App Store and Google Play proceeds in USD or other foreign currency indefinitely, may convert at its commercial discretion, and may hold offshore settlement accounts. Only general record-keeping duties apply: FINTRAC large-transaction and suspicious-transaction reporting for deposits and transfers over CAD 10,000 (or equivalent), and Statistics Canada balance-of-payments surveys where the transaction qualifies. No penalty applies for non-conversion, and there is no statutory deadline for bringing export receipts into Canada.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (partner capital contribution holdback) / Operational Account (CAD and USD clearing)
Operational Account (CAD) + USD Clearing Account via TD Bank, N.A. (US ABA and SWIFT)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High as a disbursement and multi-currency overlay; Low-Medium as the primary treasury or capital-concentration layer. Canada does not issue EU-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licences; non-bank cross-border payment providers operate as Money Service Businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Providers such as Wise, Payoneer, Stripe, Nuvei, dLocal and Airwallex can hold client funds in segregated trust accounts at regulated deposit-taking institutions and issue virtual multi-currency accounts, but they are not licensed deposit-takers, their balances are not CDIC-insured, and they cannot serve as the statutory bank account for capital-injection documentation, audit confirmation, or the LP's regulatory profile. Given the target payment rails (Apple_App_Store_Payout and Google_Play_Payout), the recommended architecture is: (i) a Schedule I bank account for all partner capital, operating cash and tax repository; (ii) a US-dollar clearing account (ABA and SWIFT) at the bank's US affiliate or a US partner bank to accept App Store and Google Play settlement; and (iii) a FINTRAC-registered MSB/EMI only for vendor disbursements in emerging-market currencies where the primary bank lacks a local clearing footprint.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted and is the market standard for a BC Limited Partnership. FINTRAC's client-identification regime allows dual-process verification (government-issued photo identification plus an independent secondary check such as a credit bureau match or liveness verification), so a director or general partner is not statutorily required to appear physically at a branch. In practice, each Schedule I bank will require: (a) a live video conference with the General Partner and at least one individual with 25% or more beneficial ownership; (b) certified true copies or notarized versions of the Certificate of Limited Partnership from BC Registry Services, the Declaration of Partnership, and the executed Partnership Agreement; (c) the BC-registered office address and proof of the registered agent; and (d) a completed beneficial-ownership schedule consistent with the British Columbia transparency/ISC standard. A BC-resident General Partner (usually a wholly-owned BC company) reduces onboarding to standard workflow, with approval in 3 to 5 business days; a fully non-resident general partner or non-resident-limited-partner majority structure will trigger Enhanced Due Diligence and likely a video or in-person interview with the bank's International/Non-Resident Commercial Desk, extending the timeline to 7 to 14 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated source of funds for the LP capital account, particularly a large inbound SWIFT from a non-resident limited partner under an undocumented mix of equity and loan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Partnership Agreement with capital commitment schedule; Certificate of Limited Partnership and Declaration from BC Registry Services; a capital contribution notice identifying exact wiring fields and subscribed units; 12-month statements from the funding institution; audited or reviewed financial statements of each contributing partner; signed source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; tax identification numbers for each partner; and the LP's beneficial-ownership schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete beneficial-ownership transparency on the BC Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) standard, or a corporate partner that itself has an opaque ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed ISC register or LP-equivalent beneficial-ownership schedule; full corporate organization chart through parent entities; certificate of good standing for each corporate partner; director/officer list for each corporate partner; residence and nationality evidence; PEP (Politically Exposed Person) status declarations; and confirmation that no individual with 25% or more control is undisclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or high-risk jurisdiction flags involving non-resident partners, overseas game development service providers, or payout corridors routed through FATF grey-listed or black-listed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Structured sanctions screening results against United Nations, Government of Canada (Special Economic Measures Act and Justice Canada consolidated sanctions), OFAC, and European Union lists; PEP and adverse-media clearance memos; proof of tax residency and physical residence for all natural-person beneficial owners; commercial rationale and signed contracts for any offshore service provider; and the BC-registered-office lease or registered-agent engagement letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume in-app purchase (IAP) aggregation risk: the bank perceives Apple and Google payout flows as third-party pass-through revenue without demonstrable commercial substance, or as an unlicensed money-service activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; App Store Connect and Play Console periodic payout statements; revenue recognition memorandum; game publishing licence and intellectual-property ownership evidence; consolidated IAP wallet ledger mapped to individual player transactions; separation of USD clearing account from CAD operating account; live app-store listings; and a written treasury policy stating that the LP is the commercial principal, not a payment intermediary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 to the LP's designated Schedule I bank account (CAD Operating Account or USD Capital Escrow Account). Canada requires no central-bank pre-authorisation for inbound capital, but the remittance instructions must be unambiguous for FINTRAC and Statistics Canada verification: Field 50K (Ordering Institution and ordering customer exactly as per KYC records), Field 57A/59 (beneficiary bank and LP account), and Field 70 (Remittance Information) stating e.g. 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - CA_LP - SUBSCRIPTION OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP UNITS'. The LP should maintain a capital contribution register that maps each wire to the subscribed units and the Partnership Agreement capital schedule. For App Store and Google Play settlement, the practical rail is a US-dollar clearing account at the bank's US affiliate (e.g. RBC Bank US or TD Bank, N.A.) or a US partner bank with ABA routing; accumulated USD balances are then swept to the Canadian CAD account at commercial spot rates. All inbound flows are subject only to standard KYC, sanctions screening, and FINTRAC reporting thresholds; no export-proceeds or conversion rules apply.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements use the following clearing rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 (and MT202 for bank-to-bank cover) for international vendor payments such as game engine licences, advertising spend, cloud hosting, remote payroll, and outsourcing contracts, with clear sanctions-scrubbed payment instructions; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) issued through RBC, Scotiabank or BMO trade desks for physical procurement such as server hardware, data-centre equipment, or large infrastructure contracts, although LC usage is expected to be limited for an ISIC 5820 digital software publisher; (c) Lynx (Payments Canada's high-value real-time settlement system) for same-day CAD transfers above the ACSS threshold; (d) EFT/ACSS batch settlement for recurring low-value Canadian payments such as payroll and Software-as-a-Service subscriptions; and (e) Interac e-Transfer for instant small-value domestic disbursements, with the Real-Time Rail (RTR) expected to become the future instant-payment utility once Payments Canada completes its build. Every disbursement must carry an unambiguous commercial invoice reference and pass through the bank's OFAC/Canadian-sanctions screening; the LP must retain an auditable open-items ledger to distinguish operating payments from capital distributions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (USD/CAD and EUR/CAD) with maturities up to 12 months, executed under a commercial hedge-only mandate with a Schedule I Canadian bank.
European-style plain vanilla FX options (call/put on USD/CAD) transacted over the counter under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted-deliverability currencies (e.g. offshore CNH, INR, IDR, PHP, ARS) to hedge emerging-market revenue and ad-spend corridors derived from global MMORPG operations.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD) with tenors of 1 to 5 years to hedge long-term partner capital, acquisition liabilities, or large infrastructure commitments.
FX swap and rolling-forward structures aligned to the weekly or monthly sweeps of Apple App Store and Google Play USD payout balances into the CAD operating account.

Bank-approved hedging-only utilization, with no speculative leverage, subject to the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, any required Credit Support Annex, and the bank's non-bank counterparty credit approval for the Limited Partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report – British Columbia Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registries and Online Services, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: due within two months after the registration anniversary date (in practice, by the last day of the month following the anniversary month).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge may apply; if default continues, the Registrar may cancel or dissolve the limited partnership registration. Administrative dissolution removes limited-liability protection and the capacity to carry on business until formal reinstatement is completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal statutory filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the later of 31 March and three months after the partnership fiscal period-end; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the return is due on 31 March annually.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Income Tax Act s. 162(7), penalty of the greater of CAD 1,000 and CAD 100 per day of default; interest on unpaid amounts and gross-negligence penalties may also apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandated for British Columbia limited partnerships under the Partnership Act. A certified audit is triggered only by the partnership agreement, lender or investor covenants, CRA requirement, or if the LP were to become a reporting issuer (not applicable for a private MMORPG publishing LP).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) as Canadian local GAAP applies; IFRS applies if the LP is publicly accountable or if the general partner elects its use.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual beneficial-ownership registry filing exists for BC limited partnerships. Beneficial-ownership particulars are updated via Notice of Change to the Registrar upon any transfer of partnership interests, capital contribution changes, and partner admissions or withdrawals. The LP must maintain an internal register identifying each limited and general partner, their capital contributions and agreed profit shares. If the LP holds an estate in land in BC, a Land Owner Transparency Report (LOTR) is required upon acquisition or change; no landholding is assumed for this MMORPG publisher.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (capital contributions and profit-share entitlements)
Register of General Partners (identity, residential address, authority)
Minute Book (limited partner meetings and general partner decisions)
Copy of Statement of Registration and all filed amendments

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 110–370 per annum (CAD 150–500) for a BC registered-office or registered-agency service; lower end for a simple registered-office address, higher end for full agent and corporate secretarial support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,900–11,000 (CAD 4,000–15,000) for a contracted voluntary audit or review of a private game-publishing LP; no mandatory audit fee otherwise.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Not applicable at the British Columbia limited partnership level because a Canadian limited partnership is generally fiscally transparent. Income is allocated to partners and taxed at partner level. Where income is earned by a taxable Canadian corporation, the combined general corporate rate is generally 27%: 15% federal and 12% British Columbia. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation may generally access a combined small-business rate of 11% on eligible income within the applicable business limit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general entity-level tax holiday applies to the limited partnership. Available incentives may include the federal Scientific Research and Experimental Development program, British Columbia research and development incentives, the federal interactive digital media tax credit, and applicable British Columbia digital-media or production credits, subject to statutory qualification, expenditure, ownership, labour, certification, and filing conditions. Partnership allocations retain their character where permitted and are generally reported by partners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CRA Form T5013, Partnership Information Return, including applicable T5013 slips and summary; electronic filing through the Canada Revenue Agency's My Business Account or Represent a Client portal, generally using CRA-approved tax software or an authorized electronic transmitter.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due within five months after the partnership fiscal period-end. A partnership with a December 31 year-end generally files by May 31 of the following year. Partnership slips must be prepared and provided to partners within the prescribed CRA deadline, generally aligned with the information-return filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business number, T5013 program account, partnership type, fiscal period, Canadian and foreign addresses, and contact information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the Canadian partnership's registered address and Canadian business number. Identify all non-resident partners and maintain their tax-residency, ownership, capital, and beneficial-ownership records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, partner classifications, partnership percentages, partner identifiers, and changes in partners during the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the correct foreign address and jurisdiction. Obtain Canadian tax identification information where required and distinguish legal partners, beneficial owners, nominees, and ultimate owners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue, cost of goods sold, operating expenses, financial expenses, assets, liabilities, capital accounts, and reconciliation to accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Canadian-dollar reporting and consistent accounting policies. Separately identify Canadian-source revenue, foreign-source revenue, related-party amounts, royalties, interest, payment-platform receipts, refunds, chargebacks, and taxes collected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss and its allocation among general and limited partners under the partnership agreement and applicable tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income using a legally supportable agreement and tax computation. Confirm at-risk limits, limited-partner loss restrictions, specified-member rules, and whether the allocation has substantial economic effect under Canadian law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner-level amounts such as business income or loss, capital gains, interest, dividends, foreign income, foreign taxes, deductions, and other income or loss categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide each non-resident partner with the applicable T5013 information and identify amounts potentially subject to Canadian withholding, Part XIII reporting, treaty claims, or partner-level Canadian income-tax filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable information concerning foreign income, foreign taxes, foreign assets, and specified foreign property where reporting is required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not assume that non-resident partners are exempt from all Canadian information reporting. Determine reporting by partner status, Canadian residence, partnership ownership, and the nature and location of the assets and income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GST/HST registration, taxable supplies, collected tax, input tax credits, and filing information where the partnership carries on a taxable activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess registration for Canadian digital supplies, in-app purchases, platform-facilitated sales, and direct sales. Apple or Google collection does not automatically eliminate all Canadian GST/HST analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Not ordinarily filed by the limited partnership itself. A Canadian corporate partner files T2 for its allocated partnership income; a non-resident corporation may have a T2 obligation if it carries on business in Canada or otherwise has a Canadian filing requirement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Determine whether a non-resident corporate partner has a Canadian permanent establishment, carries on business in Canada, disposes of taxable Canadian property, or is subject to withholding and section 216 or other specialized filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T1 General or non-resident individual return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Individual partners report allocated partnership income or loss on their Canadian individual income-tax returns where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident individual should assess Canadian-source income, carrying-on-business status, treaty protection, permanent establishment or fixed-base concepts, and any required Canadian return even where tax withheld is intended as a final tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T4, T4A, NR4, T5, and payroll remittances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information slips and source deductions for employees, contractors, Canadian dividends, interest, royalties, and other reportable payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use NR4 reporting for applicable Canadian-source amounts paid to non-residents and apply Part XIII withholding at payment or credit, whichever occurs first. Register for payroll where employees perform services in Canada.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of a T5013 partnership information return can attract a penalty generally calculated at CAD 25 per day, subject to a minimum and maximum prescribed by the Income Tax Act and CRA administrative rules, commonly a CAD 100 minimum and CAD 2,500 maximum. Additional penalties may apply for failure to file electronically when electronic filing is mandatory, failure to provide slips, inaccurate or incomplete information, repeated failures, gross negligence, unpaid withholding, and interest on overdue amounts. Directors, general partners, and responsible officers may face separate statutory liability for source deductions and other remittances.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return for a Canadian corporate partner or taxable Canadian corporate entity; CRA My Business Account or Represent a Client.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. Any balance is generally payable two months after year-end, or three months after year-end for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations, subject to statutory conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business number, corporation name, taxation year, province of residence, corporation type, and tax elections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify Canadian permanent establishments, Canadian business activities, authorized representatives, and the relevant treaty position. A non-resident corporation must not omit a T2 merely because it has no Canadian tax payable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting income to income for tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for non-deductible expenses, capital cost allowance, reserves, foreign exchange, partnership allocations, withholding taxes, and transfer-pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax calculation, corporate tax rates, provincial allocation, and federal and provincial tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the correct general, small-business, investment, or other rate. Do not claim Canadian-controlled private corporation benefits without satisfying ownership and control tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related corporations, associated corporations, ownership, and control information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign related parties and associated enterprises accurately. Reconcile all related-party amounts to Form T106 and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder and ownership information required by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report ultimate ownership and non-resident control accurately. Corporate nominee arrangements do not remove beneficial-ownership and anti-avoidance obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable income among Canadian provinces and territories based on applicable factors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income based on the location of permanent establishments and prescribed payroll and revenue factors. A British Columbia registration alone does not establish that all income is allocable to British Columbia.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing generally attracts the greater of 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per complete month late, up to 12 months, subject to statutory rules, or prescribed minimum penalties where no tax is payable. Gross-negligence penalties, repeated-failure penalties, instalment interest, arrears interest, failure-to-file penalties, and penalties for inaccurate related-party disclosures may apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Part XIII withholding remittance and NR4 information return through CRA My Business Account or Represent a Client; applicable forms include NR301, NR302, and NR303 for treaty-residency and beneficial-ownership support.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Amounts withheld are generally remitted by the 15th day of the month following the month in which the amount was paid or credited. NR4 information returns and slips are generally due by March 31 following the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend, interest, royalty, management fee, pension, rent, or other Canadian-source payment classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify by substance and source. A payment labelled as a service fee may be a royalty, rent, interest substitute, or business payment under Canadian domestic law and the applicable treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross payment or credit amount before withholding, converted to Canadian dollars using a supportable exchange-rate method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply withholding at payment or credit, including constructive credit, and retain exchange-rate evidence and payment-platform settlement records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic or treaty-reduced rate and amount remitted to CRA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply a reduced treaty rate only where residence, beneficial ownership, entitlement to treaty benefits, and required documentary evidence are established before payment or credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recipient name, address, country code, identification information where required, income code, gross income, and tax withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the beneficial recipient's information, not merely an intermediary's information, and reconcile NR4 data to the general ledger, bank records, and partnership allocations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or deficient remittances may attract penalties generally ranging from 10% to 20% of the amount required to be remitted, depending on circumstances and recurrence, plus arrears interest. Failure to withhold can create primary liability for the payer, interest, penalties, gross-negligence exposure, director liability for prescribed amounts, and potential criminal prosecution for wilful non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Canadian domestic Part XIII rules for dividends paid or credited to a non-resident. A treaty commonly reduces the rate to 15% for a portfolio dividend and 5% where the treaty ownership and corporate-shareholder conditions are satisfied. A limited partnership distribution is not automatically a dividend; its Canadian withholding result depends on the legal and tax character of the underlying amount, including business income, interest, royalties, rent, or dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment or credit, obtain reliable evidence that the recipient is resident in a treaty jurisdiction, is the beneficial owner, is entitled to treaty benefits, and satisfies any limitation-on-benefits or ownership conditions. Use Form NR301 for individuals and other non-corporate recipients, NR302 for partnerships, and NR303 for hybrid entities where applicable. Retain a current certificate of residence or equivalent evidence, ownership charts, partnership agreements, tax forms, and beneficial-ownership certifications. The payer remains responsible for reasonable due diligence; CRA pre-approval is generally not required for ordinary treaty-rate withholding. Where entitlement is uncertain, withhold at 25% and pursue an application for refund or advance CRA guidance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Part XIII withholding is generally 25% for Canadian-source royalties and interest paid or credited to non-residents, subject to statutory exemptions and treaty relief. Under the Canada-U.S. treaty, arm's-length interest is generally 0%, while royalties are commonly 10%, subject to category-specific rules. Many Canadian treaties provide 10% for royalties and 10% or 15% for interest, although rates vary by treaty and payment type. Participating debt, related-party interest, thin-capitalization rules, deemed interest, IP withholding, and treaty anti-abuse rules must be reviewed separately.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 10,000,000 of gross revenue generally triggers the Canadian documentation exception threshold analysis for contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation, but documentation is required where the statutory conditions otherwise apply to non-arm's-length cross-border transactions. Canada does not use a single transaction-value threshold that universally eliminates the arm's-length requirement. Form T106 reporting is generally required for reportable non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents, subject to prescribed exceptions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no standalone general Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance remains relevant through the arm's-length principle, the general anti-avoidance rule in section 245, beneficial-ownership and treaty anti-abuse principles, sham and substance-over-form doctrines, specified anti-avoidance rules, foreign accrual property income rules, thin-capitalization rules, and principal-purpose or limitation-on-benefits provisions under applicable treaties. A Canadian LP conducting global MMORPG publishing should maintain real Canadian functions, personnel, decision-making, development or publishing activities, contractual authority, risk control, assets, records, and commercially supportable profit allocation. Apple and Google platform settlements must be reconciled to contractual revenue ownership and transfer-pricing positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false tax reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Apple or Google receipts, omitting in-app purchase revenue, fabricating expenses, backdating partnership allocations, using false invoices, or intentionally understating Canadian-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties can include 50% of the understated tax or improperly claimed credit, reassessment of tax, interest, and denial of deductions. Criminal tax evasion can result in fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment of up to five years under the Income Tax Act, with more serious Criminal Code exposure in appropriate cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and responsible directors or officers may face personal liability for source deductions and other statutory remittances, civil recovery, prosecution, and imprisonment where personal participation or authorization is proven. Canadian law does not impose an automatic travel ban for tax debt; travel restrictions require a specific legal basis or court order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit non-resident tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying Canadian-source royalties, interest, rent, dividends, or other Part XIII amounts to foreign owners without withholding, or applying treaty rates without residency and beneficial-ownership evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for the unremitted withholding, arrears interest, late-remittance penalties, gross-negligence penalties, and costs of collection. False NR4 information or intentional non-remittance may support criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for prescribed source deductions and remittances under the Income Tax Act where statutory due-diligence defenses are unavailable. General partners may also face direct exposure under partnership and tax law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Shifting MMORPG IP profits to a low-tax affiliate without functions or risk capacity, charging unsupported royalties, using non-arm's-length platform fees, or failing to file Form T106 and contemporaneous records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may make a transfer-pricing adjustment, impose a 10% transfer-pricing penalty on relevant adjusted amounts where statutory conditions are met, deny deductions, assess withholding, apply interest, and invoke the general anti-avoidance rule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may face civil recovery and, where records are knowingly false or conduct is wilful, criminal prosecution. Liability is not automatic solely because a transfer-pricing adjustment is made.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, treaty shopping, or beneficial-ownership abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing royalties, interest, or distributions through an entity that lacks commercial substance, is not the beneficial owner, or exists primarily to obtain an unintended treaty reduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may deny treaty benefits, apply the 25% domestic withholding rate, reassess tax and interest, impose penalties, and apply the treaty's principal-purpose, limitation-on-benefits, or Canadian general anti-avoidance provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly implement false residency or beneficial-ownership representations may face civil penalties, director or officer liability for statutory remittances, and criminal consequences for fraud or false statements. No automatic corporate veil piercing occurs merely because an entity has limited substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: GST/HST and British Columbia PST non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to assess registration and collection obligations for digital games, virtual goods, subscriptions, or direct Canadian sales, or treating platform collection as conclusive without reviewing contractual responsibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Uncollected GST/HST or PST, interest, late-filing penalties, failure-to-register penalties, denial of input tax credits, audit assessments, and penalties for false returns may apply. Platform-specific marketplace rules must be tested against the actual supply chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for GST/HST amounts collected or required to be remitted where statutory due diligence is not established. General partners may face partnership-level and personal exposure under applicable legislation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Treating employees as independent game developers, withholding no payroll deductions, failing to issue T4 slips, or misclassifying Canadian workers performing core development or publishing functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The entity may owe unremitted income-tax deductions, Canada Pension Plan contributions, Employment Insurance premiums, interest, penalties, reassessed benefits, and employment-law amounts. Deliberate false reporting may support criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for employee source deductions and certain payroll remittances. Officers may face prosecution for wilful non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting suspicious payment flows, concealing beneficial owners, bypassing sanctions screening, processing proceeds from fraud or cybercrime, or failing to maintain required records where the business falls within a regulated reporting sector.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include transaction blocking, asset restraint or forfeiture, administrative monetary penalties, FINTRAC reporting failures, prosecution under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and Criminal Code offences. Sanctions breaches may produce substantial fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and general partners may be prosecuted for knowing participation, counselling, or wilful blindness. Assets may be restrained or forfeited; travel restrictions are not automatic but may arise from bail conditions, warrants, or court orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining undisclosed nominee partners, inaccurate limited-partner registers, missing significant-control information, or using partnership agreements inconsistent with actual conduct and allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties, reassessments, denial of limited-partner tax treatment, loss of statutory protections, corporate or partnership compliance orders, and potential offences under federal or British Columbia corporate legislation may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A limited partner may risk loss of limited-liability protection if it participates in control contrary to applicable partnership law. General partners have broader exposure for partnership obligations. Directors and officers may face statutory penalties and civil claims for inaccurate records.
